## Natural history notes

A small bluet damselfly characterized by its slender body, clear wings held together over the back, and blue-and-black patterning, with mature males showing a distinctive cherry-colored or reddish cast on parts of the body. In Florida, it is found around freshwater ponds, marshes, wet prairies, lakes, and slow wetland edges with emergent vegetation. Adults perch low on grasses and stems and hunt tiny flying insects, while the aquatic nymphs live among submerged plants or debris and feed on small aquatic invertebrates.
